title: introduce circuit-respite: staggered rejoin + tenant drain windows
author: Asha Patel
commits: refactor(circuit): extract state machine for 'respite' lifecycle
feat(controller): staggered rejoin scheduler and backoff policy
feat(runtime): tenant_draining window and admission gate
test: add end-to-end canary with weighted rejoin
docs: operational runbook and config knobs
release_notes: Adds a new 'circuit-respite' feature that phases tenants back into serving after circuit trips using a staggered rejoin schedule and tenant drain windows. Improves stability during region-wide recoveries and reduces mass-reopen spikes.
description:
Motivation: During a recent region-wide transient (SUP-4021) we observed large clusters of circuits flipping open->closed simultaneously which caused a follow-on traffic spike and repeated KV thrash. This change introduces 'circuit-respite' — a controlled rejoin protocol that spaces tenant re-entry and optionally drains existing sessions to smooth load.

What this PR does: Implements a staggered rejoin scheduler plus tenant drain windows and a short probationary warmup for tenants coming out of circuit trips. The key pieces: 1) runtime/circuit_manager.go: adds a RespiteState machine that tracks 'respite_start', 'scheduled_rejoin', 'probation', and 'active' states and exposes admission gates for the serving runtime; 2) controller/rejoin_scheduler.go: global controller that creates weighted rejoin cohorts based on tenant weight and recent-error fingerprint and schedules rejoin windows with jitter; 3) controller/tenant_drain.go: utilities to mark live connections as 'drainable' with a TTL and soft-evict policy to reduce sudden pressure when cohorts rejoin; 4) telemetry updates (slo_anchors) to emit RejoinCohort, DrainWindow, and ProbationLatencySample metrics; 5) Helm values and a new runtime flag (respite.enabled, respite.cohort_size, respite.cooldown_ms) to control behavior per deployment.

Design notes: The scheduler uses probabilistic cohort selection to avoid correlated reopens and includes a randomized jitter to prevent alignment across regions. Cohort size is configurable and defaults to 5% of active tenants when running in hosted mode. Probation duration is adaptive: a fast path for low-latency tenants and a conservative path for heavy KV tenants. All defaults are conservative to avoid any production regressions.

Testing: Unit tests cover state transitions and admission gate semantics (runtime/circuit_manager_test.go). Added an e2e canary script (scripts/e2e/rejoin_canary.sh) that simulates a coordinated circuit trip and measures downstream SLOs under staggered v. immediate rejoin. Ran the canary against perf-canary infra and observed a 42% reduction in 95th percentile latency spike during warmup compared to immediate reopen. CI: ci/checks/rejoin-smoke.yml validates config parsing, scheduler dry-run, and telemetry emission.

Rollout plan: Feature off by default. Deploy helm values with respite.enabled=false, then enable in dedicated staging with respite.cohort_size=0.03 and respite.cooldown_ms=30000 for a 2-week soak. Next, enable canary route for 1% of traffic using weighted-rejoin canary in controller. If telemetry shows RejoinCohortDropRate < 0.5% and ProbationLatencySample stable, gradually increase to 100%. We also added a kill-switch (respite.enabled=false) and an operator endpoint /admin/respite/abort to immediately flush all scheduled rejoins.

Operational considerations: Documented runbook in docs/operational/circuit-respite.md including steps to abort, temporarily raise cohort jitter, and read key telemetry anchors. Telemetry anchors are wired into the SLO alerting playbook so that long probation latency triggers an SRE paging rule.

Review conversation summary: Ethan: asked for clarity on cohort selection and failure amplification risk; replied with additional tests and a simulation harness (included). Marta: requested stronger invariants around admission gates to prevent overlap with existing throttlers — added gate priority ordering and unit tests. Jun: suggested adding an operator abort endpoint and a Helm flag to control canary route size — both were added.

CI and merge: The PR initially hit a flaky telemetry test (telemetry/slo_anchors test) which caused one CI rerun; after fixing the mock timing the CI passed. Reviewed and approved by all reviewers on 2026-01-20. Merged by squash on 2026-01-21.

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps default behavior conservative; we expect follow-ups to iterate on cohort heuristics and to expose richer routing controls for enterprise Dedicated flows.
notes_for_security_team: Feature introduces an operator endpoint /admin/respite/abort; endpoint requires existing operator RBAC role and a feature flag. No new data plane credentials or tenant secrets are exposed.
changelog_entry: Introduce circuit-respite: staggered tenant rejoin and drain windows to reduce reopen-induced surge. Off by default; opt-in via helm/runtime flags.
